title: Unread: what the Andean khipus say beyond numbers
summary: Many khipus record numbers in base-10 knots, but how non-numeric information was encoded is disputed, and some features are thought to form an undeciphered system.
why: An empire ran on knotted cords; if they held narratives, a whole history is waiting to be read.
question: Did Andean knotted-cord khipus record words and stories as well as numbers?
evidence: Just under 1,400 pre-Columbian khipus known; Locke showed base-10 positional numbers; Hyland's phonetic reading uses colonial-era cords.
wouldSettle: A pre-conquest khipu matched to a known written text, letting non-numeric features be read and tested.

theories.name: Binary coding (Urton)
theories.idea: Cord features form a binary system that could record sounds or word-signs.

theories.name: Meaning without sounds (Salomon)
theories.idea: Khipus were semasiographic: their signs carried meaning without encoding speech.

theories.name: Phonetic reading (Hyland)
theories.idea: Some khipus record sounds, though her examples are colonial and may reflect European influence.
